why.heading: Understanding Search Behavior in Dubai
why.body: Dubai search behavior is hyper-local and multilingual. People search by community, Marina, JLT, Deira, Mirdif, and expect results within minutes of their location. The expat majority searches primarily in English but high-value segments search in Arabic, Hindi, or other languages, and Google blends these signals in ways generic SEO misses. Commercial intent is extremely high, which drives up competition and makes the map pack brutally contested. Review velocity and recency carry unusual weight with transient populations who trust recent proof over old reputation. Local SEO packages in Dubai have to operate at neighbourhood granularity, in the right languages, with relentless review momentum.

faqs.q: Should my Dubai business target English or Arabic SEO?
faqs.a: Both, weighted by your customers. English covers the expat majority for most services, but Arabic opens the Emirati segment and huge regional trust. I assess your actual customer mix in the audit and build the language strategy around it, with proper hreflang so neither version cannibalises the other.

faqs.q: How important are Google reviews in Dubai?
faqs.a: Critical, and recency matters more here than anywhere I work. Transient populations discount old reviews, so a steady stream of fresh ones is non-negotiable. I set up a simple always-on review process as part of every package.

faqs.q: Do you need to be in Dubai to do SEO for Dubai?
faqs.a: No. Local SEO is research plus execution, and I have ranked businesses in markets I have never set foot in by studying how each community searches. What matters is the work: profile optimisation, review systems, local content, and technical soundness. All of it is done remotely, reported transparently.

faqs.q: How long do local SEO packages take to work in Dubai?
faqs.a: Map-pack movement typically starts in two to three months, with meaningful results in four to six. The most contested communities take longer, which is why we prioritise your highest-value villages first instead of boiling the ocean.
